items.a: ghfind is a developer-scoring and discovery tool for GitHub. It rates any account from 0 to 100 for real contribution value and trustworthiness using a fully deterministic, open-source engine, then adds an optional AI-written roast, head-to-head battles, and a ranked developer directory.

The engine scores six weighted dimensions that sum to 100 — account maturity, original and led project quality, contribution quality, ecosystem impact, community influence, and activity authenticity — and subtracts penalties for red flags such as PR farming or star inflation. It runs only on public GitHub data.

items.q: Is the score deterministic and reproducible?
items.a: Yes. No LLM touches the number: the same inputs always produce the same score. The scoring core is open-sourced as the github-account-value skill (AGPL), so anyone can reproduce or audit a result. Only the optional roast text is LLM-written.

items.q: Can I use ghfind via API, CLI, or MCP?
items.a: Yes. There is a public REST API (see /openapi.json), official npm and PyPI packages plus a CLI, and a Model Context Protocol server at /mcp exposing score_user, scan_user, compare_users, get_leaderboard, and search_users tools. The score endpoint needs no authentication.

items.q: Does ghfind detect bots and AI-farmed accounts?
items.a: It flags the patterns that separate farmed activity from honest work — near-identical template PR titles, contributions concentrated on repos the account doesn't own, and suspicious star or follower inflation. In a dataset of 18,947 scored accounts, fewer than 1% tripped the strongest red flags — rare, but extreme when present.

No. Scores use public signals only, so private-organization contributions are invisible to the engine. An active member of private repos may be underrated. A low score is not a factual claim about a person — it describes an account's public footprint.

homeIntro.whatBody: ghfind is a developer-scoring and discovery tool for GitHub. It rates any account from 0 to 100 across six weighted dimensions — account maturity, original and led project quality, contribution quality, ecosystem impact, community influence, and activity authenticity — using a fully deterministic engine (the open-source github-account-value skill, AGPL). The same inputs always produce the same score; no LLM touches the number. On top of the score it adds an optional AI-written roast, developer-vs-developer battles, language and organization leaderboards, and README score badges.

steps.title: 1. Scan the public footprint
steps.body: Enter any GitHub username. The engine crawls the account's public data — repositories, pull requests, issues, stars, followers — and builds an evidence snapshot. No login and no permissions are required.

steps.title: 2. Score six deterministic dimensions
steps.body: The snapshot is scored across account maturity, original and led project quality, contribution quality, ecosystem impact, community influence, and activity authenticity, with penalties for PR-farming, star inflation, and template-spam patterns.

steps.title: 3. Get your adventurer level, realm, and roast
steps.body: You get a reproducible adventurer level (Lv.1–100), a cultivation realm from Qi Condensation to Grand Ascension, a per-dimension breakdown showing exactly what holds the score down, and — only if you ask for it — a witty, fair AI-written roast.

about.metaDescription: ghfind scores any GitHub account 0-100 for real contribution value and trust with an open-source, deterministic engine, and helps you discover top developers.
about.heading: About ghfind
paragraphs: ghfind is a developer-scoring and discovery tool for GitHub. It rates any account from 0 to 100 for real contribution value and trustworthiness, using a fully deterministic engine that runs only on public GitHub data. The same inputs always produce the same score — no large language model is involved in the number itself — so results are reproducible and auditable rather than opaque.

The score is built from six weighted dimensions that sum to 100: account maturity, original and led project quality, contribution quality, ecosystem impact, community influence, and activity authenticity. On top of that factual core, ghfind adds an optional AI-written roast, developer-versus-developer battles, leaderboards by programming language, organization, and project, and README score badges you can embed on your own profile.

The scoring engine is open source under the AGPL license as the github-account-value skill, and the same code paths power the website, the official npm and PyPI packages, the command-line tool, and the Model Context Protocol server. ghfind exists to make GitHub contribution legible: to reward genuine open-source work, surface developers worth following, and make farmed or faked activity easy to spot by looking at patterns instead of raw counts.

contact.metaDescription: How to reach the ghfind team: report an issue, or ask about the API, CLI, and MCP server.
contact.heading: Contact
paragraphs: ghfind is an open-source project. The fastest way to reach the team, report a problem, or ask about the API, CLI, or MCP server is to open an issue on the public GitHub repository. Issues are read and triaged there, and keeping the conversation in the open helps other users who hit the same question.

For integration questions, the machine-readable API contract lives at /openapi.json, the agent-facing documentation index at /llms.txt, and the authentication walkthrough at /auth.md. If you need an elevated rate limit for high-volume server-to-server scanning, mention your use case in a GitHub issue.
contact.bizLead: For business inquiries, bulk licensing, or elevated API rate limits, email us directly:
contact.bizNote: (For open-source usage questions, please prefer a GitHub issue — public answers help other users too.)

privacy.metaDescription: How ghfind handles data: it scores only public GitHub data and does not sell personal data.
privacy.heading: Privacy

sections.p: ghfind computes scores from public GitHub data only — the same information anyone can see on a profile and its public repositories, pull requests, and activity. It does not access private repositories, private contributions, email contents, or any data that is not already public on GitHub. Because of this, scores describe an account's public footprint and are not a factual claim about the person behind it.

For accounts that are scored, we cache the computed score, tier, and derived metrics so shared reports load quickly and the leaderboard stays fast. Only accounts scoring 60 or above are indexed and listed publicly; lower-scoring pages are reachable by direct link but kept out of search engines. We use privacy-respecting, aggregate analytics to understand traffic and do not sell personal data.

If you choose Google sign-in, we receive your Google account identifier (subject), name and profile image to establish your ghfind session. Google may also return your email address during sign-in; we do not persist it. A signed, HttpOnly session cookie stores your basic identity for up to 30 days. We do not retain Google API access tokens or refresh tokens. Signing out clears the session cookie. Google sign-in does not grant GitHub permissions, and we do not automatically link accounts by email address.

The optional roast feature can use your own model provider key. When you supply one, it stays in your browser and is relayed once through our server to call the model — it is never stored and never logged, and is discarded after the request completes.

When we show ads, third-party vendors, including Google, use cookies, web beacons, and similar technologies to serve ads based on your prior visits to this site or other sites. Google's use of advertising cookies enables it and its partners to serve ads to you based on your visit to this site and/or other sites on the Internet. You can opt out of personalized advertising by visiting Google Ads Settings (https://adssettings.google.com). To opt out of some third-party vendors' uses of cookies for personalized advertising, visit www.aboutads.info/choices.

methodology.metaTitle: Methodology — how ghfind scores GitHub accounts
methodology.metaDescription: How ghfind's deterministic engine scores GitHub accounts across six weighted dimensions, applies red-flag penalties, and stays fully reproducible without any LLM.
methodology.heading: How ghfind scores GitHub accounts
methodology.lead: ghfind's score is produced by a deterministic rubric, not a model. The engine reads public GitHub data, scores six dimensions that sum to 100, subtracts penalties for red flags, and returns the same number every time for the same inputs. The core is open source under the AGPL license, so any result can be reproduced and audited.
methodology.dimensionsIntro: Each dimension contributes to the 100-point base score. Together they reward sustained, original, widely-used open-source work over raw activity counts.

dimensionDetails.account_maturity: How established and consistent the account is over time — age, sustained activity, and a credibility curve that resists overnight inflation.
dimensionDetails.original_project_quality: Quality and reception of personally authored projects and substantially led or co-built projects, weighted by attribution share; excludes forks.
dimensionDetails.contribution_quality: The substance of contributions to other projects — merged, meaningful pull requests versus template spam.
dimensionDetails.ecosystem_impact: How much the account's work is depended on and maintained across the wider ecosystem.
dimensionDetails.community_influence: Genuine reach and standing in the community, normalized so raw follower or star counts cannot dominate.
dimensionDetails.activity_authenticity: Whether activity patterns look organic or engineered — the dimension that separates honest work from farming.

methodology.penaltiesBody: On top of the six dimensions, the engine subtracts penalties for patterns that inflate a profile without real value: near-identical template pull-request titles, contributions concentrated on repositories the account does not own, and star or follower inflation. Every individual event can look plausible; the penalties fire on the pattern, which is what makes farmed activity separable from honest work.
methodology.determinismBody: No large language model touches the score. The scoring core is the open-source github-account-value skill (AGPL), and the same code paths power the website, the npm and PyPI packages, the CLI, and the MCP server. Given the same public inputs, the score is identical across all of them, which is why it can be independently reproduced. The optional roast text is the only LLM-written part and never changes the number.
methodology.dataBody: Applied to a public dataset of 18,947 scored accounts — 3,444 with full raw-metric snapshots — faked or farmed contribution turned out to be rarer than the discourse suggests (under 1% of accounts tripped the strongest red flags) but far more extreme when it appeared. The full analysis is in the research section.

githubBot.metaTitle: ghfind Review | GitHub Bot for Issue and PR triage
githubBot.metaDescription: ghfind Review combines author-score labels and content classification with previews, cleanup and your own AI service (BYOK), managed per repository.

hero.title:
Issue and PR triage,
under your control.
hero.subtitle: Label Issues and PRs by author score or content. Control automation, previews and cleanup from one Bot console.

console.heading: Your Bot workspace
console.note: Sign in with GitHub. The console shows installations and repositories you can access.

overview.title: Dashboard
overview.body: An overview across your GitHub installations.

repositories.title: Repositories
repositories.body: Configure labels and pause or resume processing.

tasks.title: Tasks
tasks.body: Follow backfills and retry failed jobs.

activity.title: Activity
activity.body: Review configuration changes and cleanup history.

console.screenshotAlt: Bot Dashboard showing installation overview, repository status, tasks and recent activity.

classification.heading: Two kinds of labels. Two different signals.
classification.lead: Keep author-profile context separate from the topic of a contribution.

score.title: Author-score labels
score.body: For new Issues and PRs, the Bot looks up the author’s public ghfind score and applies a review: label. The score describes a public profile, not the quality of the contribution.
score.example: Five score bands, including an explicit no-score label when a score is unavailable.

intent.title: Content classification
intent.body: Compare the Issue or PR title and body with descriptions of existing labels you select. When enabled, the classifier can add up to three matching labels without creating or renaming any labels.
intent.example: Requires a configured classification service. Try a suggestion in the console before enabling it. AI classification is separate from the author score and may need correction. Connect your own AI service in repository settings.

byok.heading: Use your own AI service
byok.lead: Bring your endpoint, API key and model. Configure each repository separately, then choose your service or the platform service.
byok.setup: Open a repository, then choose AI service. Saving requires repository admin access.

provider.title: Choose the service per repository
provider.body: Switch between the platform service and your own public HTTPS API base URL. Each repository keeps its own configuration.

protocol.title: Choose the protocol and model
protocol.body: OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions can classify content and generate greetings. Jev Decisions classifies content only.

key.title: Keep your key private
key.body: API keys are encrypted at rest and never shown again. Replace or remove a saved key from the console.

test.title: Test before enabling
test.body: Explicitly test the saved connection. The test makes no GitHub changes and stores no sample text. Content classification remains off by default.

byok.billing: Your provider bills requests to your key. If your own service fails, the Bot does not silently switch to the platform service.

operations.heading: Preview first. Then decide.
operations.lead: Control each repository individually, with changes recorded in the activity log.

preview.title: Test a label suggestion
preview.body: Try an Issue or PR sample against saved label definitions. The preview makes no GitHub changes and does not save your sample text. Requires a configured classification service.

backfill.title: Process existing submissions
backfill.body: Start a backfill yourself for the latest 1–100 open Issues and PRs. Installation only initializes score labels; it does not start a historical backfill.

cleanup.title: Review and undo Bot changes
cleanup.body: Preview eligible removals before confirming. Cleanup only removes changes attributable to this Bot; manually re-added labels and changes with unclear ownership are kept.

cli.heading: The same controls, from your terminal.
cli.body: Go, JavaScript and Python CLIs support status, pause, resume, backfill, retry and cleanup. Use a token with explicit Bot scopes; repository access is still required.
cli.note: The cleanup command previews removals. A separate confirmation is required to apply them.

reference.heading: Author-score labels and GitHub search filters

labels.heading: Five author-score bands
labels.lead: Missing score labels are created on install. Existing custom colors and descriptions are preserved.

top.desc: Highest band of the ghfind index.

noScore.desc: Unavailable is not zero. Transient failures are retried after 20 and 60 minutes.

queues.heading: Filter in GitHub
queues.lead: Paste a filter into your repository’s Issues search. Replace is:issue with is:pr to find pull requests.

install.heading: Start with selected repositories
install.body: Install the GitHub App with Issues and Pull requests read/write access. No repository workflow, PAT or secret is needed. Organization repositories may require owner approval.

privacy.heading: Know what is processed
privacy.body: Scoring uses the author’s public profile. Optional classification sends the title, body and selected label descriptions to the configured AI service. Comments are off by default; if enabled, they include an introduction and author-score summary, not a code review.

stop.heading: Pause or remove the Bot
stop.body: Pause processing per repository from the console, or remove the App in GitHub settings. Existing labels stay; use cleanup to review eligible Bot changes separately.

githubBot.disclaimer: The score reflects the author’s public GitHub profile, not the quality of this contribution. New contributors may simply have a short public record.

integrations.title: CLI & API
integrations.subtitle: Connect ghfind to your terminal, scripts, and agents. Install the CLI and Skill, create a personal API token, and explore the API docs.

install.heading: Install the CLI and Skill with one command
install.description: Copy this into a terminal or coding agent. Node.js 18 or newer is required; no sudo needed.
install.requirement: The script installs the official npm CLI and saves the ghfind-cli Skill to ~/.agents/skills/ghfind-cli.

how.heading: Get connected
how.install: Run the command to install the ghfind CLI.
how.skill: The installer also adds the ghfind-cli Skill so your agent can read the commands and guidance.
how.auth: For full scans or roasts, create an API token above and set GHFIND_API_KEY.

tokens.heading: Create API token
tokens.signedOut: Sign in with GitHub to create separate tokens for your CLI or automation. A token is shown only once when created.
tokens.description: Revoke tokens individually. The full token is never shown again.
tokens.scanIncluded: Every token includes scan access for the CLI, API, and MCP.
tokens.botPermissionHint: Lets this token change bot settings and run cleanups on repositories where you are an admin.
tokens.scopesUnavailableError: Bot permissions are not available yet. Try again later.
tokens.copyOnce: Copy and save it now. You cannot view the full token again after leaving this page.
tokens.loadError: Could not load tokens. Refresh and try again.
tokens.createError: Could not create the token. Try again.
tokens.limitError: You have reached the active token limit. Revoke a token you no longer use.
tokens.revokeError: Could not revoke the token. Try again.

auth.heading: Authentication
auth.description: Sign in to the website with GitHub OAuth. CLI and API requests use a personal Bearer token created from your account; these credentials are separate.
auth.public: Scoring, comparisons, search, leaderboards, and developer directories work without a token.
auth.protected: Full scans and roasts that run a scan require GHFIND_API_KEY.
auth.credentialNote: Keep tokens in environment variables or a secrets manager. Do not commit them or give them to an untrusted agent.
